name: cc-enslaver
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; three CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.32.0 closes the two items v0.31 recorded instead of fixing, both decided by the user. FIRST, Stop layer (i) now rejects a sync acknowledgement that answers nothing: `_has_sync_marker` was presence-only, so `sync-check: n/a` — and a marker the agent merely QUOTED — settled a named co-update group as firmly as a real sweep report. It now applies the two tests layer (h) already applies to `tldr`, through the same lib/mdctx model: attribution (a marker inside a non-canonical fence or a blockquote is illustrative, not a claim) and substance (the value must carry content, on its own line or the next non-blank one; a bare placeholder is treated as absent, and a non-answer cannot borrow the following line). The limit is pinned by its own test so it cannot drift into an implied guarantee: vacuous PROSE (`sync-check: checked it`) is still accepted and is not claimed to be detected, because refusing an honest report is the worse error. A deliberate strictness increase. SECOND, `check` now runs against this repository in CI. v0.31.0 shipped it arguing that an unenforced gate you still trust is worse than none, and gave it a non-zero exit specifically so it could run in CI — then never ran it on itself, the same defect one level up. Wired as a test rather than a workflow step, matching test_i18n_sync, so a local unittest run covers it too, and shipped with the twin that keeps a green check from meaning an empty config. 594 -> 601 tests. Prior — v0.31.1 folds rule 12's acknowledgement into the reply schema. Every other closing obligation (before / edits / convergence / fidelity / closing / tldr) has been a schema FIELD since v0.20, whose design is that the field name IS the Stop-hook marker; rule 12 arrived three releases later and its sync acknowledgement stayed free prose with no slot to write it in — the only duty whose omission looked like an ordinary reply. It is now `sync-check:` (zh: `同步核对:`) in all four injected prompts. Zero hook code changed: the key already matches SYNC_MARKERS. It does NOT weaken layer (i), verified by probe rather than by reading — since v0.27 a marker settles only groups a previous block actually NAMED, so a first violation still blocks and names its group, and the field is where the answer to that group goes next turn. A vacuous `sync-check: n/a` still settles a named group; that is unchanged from today's free-prose markers, is called out in both prompts, and adding a substance check would be a strictness contract change deliberately not made here. The release also found a pre-existing drift: README.zh.md's version badge said 0.29.0 at 0.31.1 — two releases stale with every gate green — because the badge check pinned README.md and not its mirror; it now discovers every README*.md from disk. 590 -> 594 tests. Prior — v0.31.0 made the rule-12 sync gate INSPECTABLE. Co-update groups have been enforceable since v0.23 and authorable only by hand-writing TOML, with no way to see what the loader made of it — and the loader is failing-open by design, so a dropped group or a glob matching no file does not raise, it just stops guarding while printing one stderr line nobody reads. An unenforced gate you still trust is worse than no gate, because you have stopped looking. The new `/cc-enslaver:sync-gate` command (init / list / check / add / remove / path) closes that: `check` reports every group the loader kept, every group it DROPPED and why, and every dead glob, exiting 1 so it runs in CI. Deliberately NOT auto-created — no hook writes into your project directory, and an auto-created empty template would be functionally identical to no file (zero groups means layer (i) stays inert) at the price of an unrequested file in everyone's git status. Writes are verified twice: not just "does this parse" but "does the loader still keep every group", because a `require = []` entry is valid TOML that load() silently discards, so a parse-only check would let the CLI report success over a group guarding nothing; on failure the previous file is restored byte-for-byte. A defect found in this feature's own first smoke test is reported rather than quietly fixed: the CLI picked its write target with the resolver built for READING, which tries several roots and takes the first that already holds a file — so run against a project with no config yet it fell through to the process cwd and wrote two groups into this plugin's own config. Root cause: "where do I read from" and "where do I write to" are different questions, and a read-resolver's fallback chain is exactly what makes it the wrong answer to the second. Fixed at the mechanism (default_project_path, deterministic; load_file, no fallback), class swept across both call sites, with the read resolver's fallback pinned too so a later "make everything deterministic" cannot silently break the hook path. lib/tomlio.py now owns the TOML writer as well as the reader, so both config CLIs share one encoder. 565 → 590 tests. Prior — v0.30.0 was a structural audit of the plugin itself, on one theme: a thing that is written down is not a thing that is enforced. Seven unreachable production symbols were deleted rather than annotated — including a retired rationale checker sitting beside the live one, where the next reader cannot tell which the guard consults, and an `_escape_triple_quoted` marked "kept only so an external caller does not break" that no caller could reach. Three duplicated judgements collapsed to one definition each: markdown fence parsing existed in three copies, each carrying its own transcription of the same v0.25 CommonMark fix, and the project-root predicate existed twice with the second annotated "same heuristic as lib/edicts.py" — a sentence that names an invariant without holding it (new: lib/projroot.py). And the Stop status table stopped lying: layers are displayed (a)-(i) but evaluated with (b) first, and the table derived both Pass and pending from the DISPLAY index, so every hedge block printed "(a) PASS" — asserting convergence evidence had been found on a turn where the evidence check never ran. A gate built to catch unfounded claims does not get to make one; fixed with twin tests in both directions. The tree was reclassified rather than rearranged (test files named for what they cover, hooks/scripts/ labelling its three roles inline, a new docs/ index), and the four non-hook scripts deliberately did NOT move to a tools/ directory: two of them are called from inside hooks, so the move would trade a tidier directory name for a real cross-tree import splice. CLAUDE.md shrank 87 KB to 39 KB — its "current version" section had become a verbatim second copy of the changelog, re-read into context on every session, and a second source that could drift. 564 → 565 tests. Full history: CHANGELOG.md.
